title: Your brain makes things up in the dark

lines.text: Stare at nothing long enough, and your brain will start inventing things to see.
It's called the Ganzfeld effect. Ganzfeld is German for complete field.
When your eyes get a perfectly uniform view, like a blank wall of light or a whiteout, there's nothing to process.
So your brain turns up the gain, and starts amplifying its own noise.
People report patterns, colours, and even full images.
In the 1930s, psychologist Wolfgang Metzger found people staring into a featureless field consistently hallucinated.
Trapped miners and Arctic explorers have described the same thing.
Your brain would rather make something up than see nothing at all.
